summary: The narrator and a companion discuss a plan to put civilians in positions where police must decide whether to treat them as terrorists, comparing it to jamming with music instead of gadgets. The conversation shifts to a Mission district burrito shop, described as cheap, huge and ugly, where the companion douses her burrito in capsaicin oil from a mister and eats it despite the narrator's disbelief.
one_line: Friends debate a civilian protest tactic, then share Mission burritos where one doses hers with capsaicin oil.
key_facts: The narrator's friends do not know that Marcus and M1k3y are the same person.
The narrator describes the plan as putting civilians in a position where police must decide whether to treat ordinary people like terrorists.
The companion compares the plan to jamming, but with music instead of gadgets.
Mission burritos are described as cheap, giant and delicious, roughly the size of a bazooka shell.
Mission burrito fillings include spicy grilled meat, guacamole, salsa, tomatoes, refried beans, rice, onions and cilantro.
The narrator says a Mission burrito has the same relationship to Taco Bell that a Lamborghini has to a Hot Wheels car.
There are about two hundred Mission burrito joints, which are decorated with faded Mexican tourist office posters and electrified framed Jesus and Mary holograms.
The place they visited served brains and tongue, which the narrator and companion did not order.
The narrator ordered carne asada and the companion ordered shredded chicken, with a big cup of horchata each.
The companion misted her burrito with capsaicin oil from a stainless-steel aerosol canister that resembled pepper spray.
The narrator says the capsaicin oil made his throat close and his eyes water.
The companion calls herself a spicy food addict and jokingly suggests the narrator think of the oil as Spicy Cajun Visine.
The narrator says the burrito was basically an anti-personnel weapon the companion had slathered on her dinner.
The companion bit into the dosed burrito, chewed and swallowed it.
